# Getting started

## What you need

1. **A copy of the website folder.** Ask the web editor for the current
   version. Keep it somewhere stable on your computer and treat it as the
   single place where edits happen.
2. **Quarto.** The free download from [quarto.org](https://quarto.org) is
   all you need to preview and render pages.
3. **A text editor.** [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/)
   is the easiest option because it has a Render button and a
   "Replace in Files" tool that the yearly setup relies on. VS Code works
   too. You do not need to write any R code for routine updates.

The full setup walkthrough, including how to get a copy of the site and the
one-time install steps, is in `UPDATING.md` under "Getting a copy of the
website" and "One-time setup".

## Previewing your work

From the project root (the folder that contains `_quarto.yml`), run:

```
quarto preview
```

This opens the site in your browser and refreshes it as you save files.
To build a single page instead:

```
quarto render conferences/index.qmd
```

Rendered pages land in the `docs/` folder. That folder is what eventually
goes live, so a quick look at your page in the browser is the best check
before you hand anything off.

## When you are finished editing

You never publish directly. When your changes look right in the preview,
share the changed files with the web editor, keeping their folder structure
intact. The exact handoff steps are in `UPDATING.md` under "How changes
reach the live site". Nothing you do in your local copy can break the live
site, so experiment freely.
